## Abstract
patches.evidence: Rendered physical p.1 (300 dpi bottom crop) prints a footnote rule followed by '*Work done while at Google.' at the bottom of the title page; OCR kept the matching '*' markers after Daniel De Freitas and Noam Shazeer in the author list but dropped the footnote body.

Rendered physical p.35 shows '3. Is B's response factually correct?' as a numbered crowdworker-instruction item followed by bullet sub-items, at the same level as siblings '1. Is the conversation understandable?' and '2. Does B's response contain any factual claims?', which the OCR kept as plain paragraphs; only this line was falsely promoted to a section heading.
Rendered physical p.7 prints the generative fine-tuning example format as “<context> <sentinel> <response>” with spaces between the angle-bracket tokens; OCR glued the tokens together.
Rendered physical p.7 prints the discriminative fine-tuning example format as “<context> <sentinel> <response> <attribute-name> <rating>” with spaces between tokens; OCR glued the tokens together.

patches.before: "<context><sentinel><response><attribute-name>"). Since the model has already processed "<context><sentinel><response>", evaluating the discriminator simply involves processing a few additional tokens: "<attribute-name><desired rating)"
patches.after: "<context> <sentinel> <response> <attribute-name>"). Since the model has already processed "<context> <sentinel> <response>", evaluating the discriminator simply involves processing a few additional tokens: "<attribute-name> <desired rating>"
patches.evidence: Physical p.7 (rendered crop plus text layer) prints “<attribute-name> <desired rating>” as the final tokens in the discriminator sentence; OCR glued the tokens and misread the closing angle bracket after 'rating' as a parenthesis.

Rendered physical p.32 (300 dpi crop of the Table 8 ethnicity block) prints 'White or Causcasian' with respondents 62; the double 's' is the print's own misspelling and OCR silently corrected it to 'Caucasian'. The safety-annotation table on p.33 prints 'Caucasian' correctly and is left unchanged.
Rendered physical p.33 (300 dpi crop of the Table 9 sexual-orientation block) prints 'Hetrosexual or straight' with respondents 72; the print's own misspelling was silently corrected by OCR.
